messages.body_plain:
Dear All,
Maybe the answer to this is a one-liner, but I need some help.
Consider the snippet at the end of the email.
The result is definitely not what I would like to achieve.
I would like to plot ml1, ml2 and ml3 as three separate lines, but ml1
and ml3 should have the same color and have the same description in the
legend.
My problem is that ml1 and ml2 get mixed up in the plot.
How can I solve that?
My original problem amounts to plotting hundreds of lines with only a
few colors (predefined groups of different lines should have the same
color), so I end up with an object like ml_tmp, hence (in the case of my
example) I would like a fix which relies on ml_tmp to plot three
distinct lines with two colors and only 2 corresponding entries in the
legend.
Can anyone help me out with this?
Many thanks

Lorenzo

####################################################
####################################################
####################################################

library(ggplot2)
library(Cairo)

ml1 <- cbind(seq(10),seq(10))
ml1 <- as.data.frame(ml1)

ml2 <- cbind(seq(20),2*seq(20))
ml2 <- as.data.frame(ml2)

ml3 <- cbind(seq(30),3*seq(30))
ml3 <- as.data.frame(ml3)

names(ml1) <- c("time","my_function")
names(ml2) <- c("time","my_function")
names(ml3) <- c("time","my_function")

ml_tmp <- rbind(transform(ml1, set="Aggregated"),
        transform(ml2, set="30 Rewirings"), transform(ml3,
set="Aggregated"))

gpl <- ggplot(ml_tmp, aes(x=time, y=my_function, colour=set, shape=set)) +
geom_line(size=0.5)

CairoPDF("Test_legend.odf")
print(gpl)
dev.off()

messages.subject: Re: Plotting Multiple Lines and Legend
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lorenzo:

Does this do what you want? I think all you need to add is a data set indicator...

ml1 <- cbind(seq(10),seq(10))
ml2 <- cbind(seq(20),2*seq(20))
ml3 <- cbind(seq(30),3*seq(30))
 ml <- as.data.frame(rbind(ml1, ml2, ml3))
> names(ml)
[1] "V1" "V2"
> dim(ml)
[1] 60  2
# data set indicator
ml$ds <- factor(rep(1:3, c(10, 20, 30)))
# factor on which to map color
ml$set <- factor(rep(c('Aggregated', '30 Rewirings', 'Aggregated'),
                      c(10, 20, 30))
# Use ds to influence shape of points, set to influence color
p1 <- ggplot(ml, aes(x = V1, y = V2, shape = ds, colour = set))
p1 + geom_point(size = 0.5) + geom_line()

To get rid of the shape legend, add scale_shape(legend = FALSE).

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: trouble with dodged plot
messages.body_plain:
Hi:

I think you want something like geom_linerange(); see if this works for you.

# Transform the data set to wide format; I've used the reshape() function often
# enough to do this fairly quickly, but melt() and cast() in Hadley's reshape package
# would also work:

dfa <- reshape(df_summary, idvar = c('type', 'group'), timevar = 'dist',
                      direction = 'wide')
names(dfa)[3:5] <- paste('Q', 1:3, sep = "")
dfa <- transform(dfa, gp = group + (as.numeric(type) - 1) * 0.1)

# This is what we have prior to the plot. Use Q2 for the y-point,
# Q1 for ymin and Q3 for ymax in the plot_linerange() call below.
# Hadley's dodging trick for the type variable is in the gp variable.

> dfa
   type group Q1 Q2 Q3  gp
1     a     1  1  4  9 1.0
4     b     1  1  4  9 1.1
7     a     2  1  4  9 2.0
10    b     2  1  4  9 2.1
13    a     3  1  4  9 3.0
16    b     3  1  4  9 3.1
19    a     4  1  4  9 4.0
22    b     4  1  4  9 4.1
25    a     5  1  4  9 5.0
28    b     5  1  4  9 5.1
31    a     6  1  4  9 6.0
34    b     6  1  4  9 6.1
# Now do the plot....
p <- ggplot(dfa, aes(x = gp, y = Q2, ymin = Q1,  ymax = Q2, colour = type))
p + geom_linerange()

Hopefully, this is what you were after if I understood your request properly.

Dennis

messages.body_plain:
After much fiddling around I finally found a solution (I actually wanted
the letters just above the upper whiskers, I got it wrong in my last
message). But is there a simpler way to do this?

# previous code

dummy <- data.frame(values = rnorm(30), fac1 = factor(rep(rep(1:3, each
= 5), 2)), fac2 = factor(rep(1:2, each = 15) ))
p <- ggplot(dummy, aes(fac1, values)) + geom_boxplot() + facet_wrap(~
fac2)
p

# solution: add letters for post-hoc Tukey results above upper whiskers
lettpos <- function(dummy)   boxplot(dummy$values)$stats[5,]
test <- ddply(dummy, .(fac2, fac1), lettpos)
test$lett <- rep("a", nrow(test))
colnames(test)[3] <- "upper"
p + geom_text(aes(fac1, upper + 0.05, label = lett), data = test, vjust
= 0)

messages.body_plain:
Hi:

I can help remove the labels on the y-axis and change the title on the legend,
but I don't know how to change the tick marks on the pie to black (and I'm not sure
you want to, because it will interfere with the numeric labels...but I digress).

I prefer to set the 'scaffolding' of the plot first and save it to an object:

pg <- ggplot(as.data.frame.table(VADeaths),
                  aes(x = factor(1), y = Freq, fill = Var1))

# Then,

pg + geom_bar(width = 1) +

      facet_wrap(~Var2, scales = "free_y") +
      coord_polar(theta = "y") +

      scale_fill_hue("Age group") +                            # change legend title
      opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank(),
           axis.text.y = theme_blank(),                        # remove y axis label
           axis.ticks = theme_blank()) +                      # remove y axis tick marks
      xlab("") + ylab("")                                             # remove pointless axis titles

This still leaves you with the problem of getting the color you want on the circumference
tick marks, but hopefully someone else can edify you on that point.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.body_plain:
I am getting some strange behavior with geom_hline when I use it with
stat_summary.  I think this is a bug, but could also be a
misunderstanding on my part about how to use stat_summary.

I want to put a horizontal line on my plots that is 10% below one of
the datapoints.  I'm going to do this over and over, so I want it to
be a stat_summary function rather than just calculating and plotting
the values.  If it use geom_hline(yintercept=2) as a layer in my
ggplot call, everything is fine.  However, when I attempt to use
geom_hline with stat_summary, it seems to expect to get values for y,
yend, etc.  My understanding is that it should only need a value for
yintercept.  Here is the code I would like to use:

tenBelow <- function(y) {
	means <- mean(y, na.rm=TRUE)
	data.frame(yintercept=means*.9)
}

tenPercLine <- function(...) {
	return(stat_summary(fun.data=tenBelow, geom='hline', color='red',
linetype='dashed', ...))
}

Since I can't get this to work, I'm using segments instead with this
code:

tenBelow <- function(y) {
	means <- mean(y, na.rm=TRUE)
	data.frame(y=means*.9, yend=means*.9, x=0, xend=15)
}

tenPercLine <- function(...) {
	return(stat_summary(fun.data=tenBelow, geom='segment', color='red',
linetype='dashed', ...))
}

This is frustrating because I have to hard code the x values (which is
inelegant), and it results in a line that does not flow off the edges
of my facets, which is undesireable.  (I thought I could get around
this by using x=-Inf and x=Inf, but not so).

Elaine McVey

Research Triangle Park, NC

messages.subject: Re: pesky legends
messages.body_plain:
One of the reasons reproducible code is nice is that it often is the
clearest way to explain a problem.

For example from your first post it wasn't clear if maybe you are
doing something like:
qplot(1:10, 1:10, size = 10)
# and are wondering why there is a "5" in the legend?
# In which case you want
qplot(1:10, 1:10, size = I(10))

# or equivalently you are doing
ggplot(data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 1:10)) + geom_point(aes(x, y, size = 5))
# and you want (Brian's point)
ggplot(data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 1:10)) + geom_point(aes(x, y), size = 5)

Or maybe you are doing something like:
qplot(1:10, 1:10, size = 1:10)
# and you just want to get rid of the legend
qplot(1:10, 1:10, size = 1:10) + opts(legend.position = "none")

Or maybe you want more control over the legend:
qplot(1:10, 1:10, size = 1:10) + scale_size(to = c(5,15))

Or maybe it's something else?  But I think perhaps the first example
is what you want.

Charlotte
